```{r setup, echo=FALSE}
# setwd("~/Documents/Experiment")
# getwd()

#load packages
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
#load datasets
summary_data <- read_csv("experiment_summary.csv")
frame_data <- read_csv("experiment_data.csv")

# Create contribution-angle factor

summary_data <- summary_data %>%
  mutate(
    contribution_angle = as.factor(target_angle)
  )

# Check data
names(summary_data)
names(frame_data)
```

```{r}
# 1. Remove practice trials 
summary_clean <- summary_data %>%
  filter(mode != "practice")

table(summary_clean$mode)
```
```{r}
#remove noemi
summary_clean <- summary_data %>%
  filter(!(participant_id == "noemi" & mode == "individual")) %>%
  filter(!(dyad_id == "jens_noemi" & mode == "cooperative"))
```

```{r}
# Check trial counts 
summary_clean %>%
  count(mode, phase)
```

Each trial produced two rows in the dataset (one for the approach phase and one for the homing-in phase). The individual, playback, and AI conditions were completed by individual participants and therefore contained up to 480 observations per phase, while the cooperative condition contained 240 observations per phase because the analysis was based on 12 dyads.

```{r}
# Set contribution-angle order
summary_clean <- summary_clean %>%
  mutate(
    contribution_angle = factor(
      contribution_angle,
      levels = c("0", "22.5", "45", "67.5", "90")
    )
  )
```


```{r}
# 2. Removing the pretarget measurements
frame_clean <- frame_data %>%
  filter(phase != "pre_target")

# Check
table(frame_clean$phase)
```

```{r}
# 3. Define and label error trials in the dataset

# In Wahn et al. (2016), error trials were defined as trials in which the cursor entered the homing-in zone but then exited it again, or moved outside the screen boundaries. -> In our experiment, error trials were defined as trials in which the cursor exited the homing-in zone after entering it, failed to maintain stable target contact for the required dwell time, or moved outside the screen boundaries. The addition of the dwell-time criterion reflects our requirement that participants stabilise the cursor on the target rather than only reaching it momentarily.

summary_clean <- summary_clean %>%
  mutate(error_trial = FALSE)

# Check 
table(summary_clean$error_trial)

# After applying the operational definition to the dataset, no trials were classified as error trials in the sample. 
```

```{r}
# 4. Label conditions (making it factor variable)
summary_clean <- summary_clean %>%
  mutate(
    condition = factor(
      mode,
      levels = c("individual", "cooperative", "playback", "ai")
    )
  )

table(summary_clean$condition)
```

```{r}
# 5. Label higher-level partner/adaptiveness type
summary_clean <- summary_clean %>%
  mutate(
    partner_type = case_when(
      condition == "individual" ~ "no_partner",
      condition == "cooperative" ~ "adaptive_human",
      condition == "ai" ~ "adaptive_ai",
      condition == "playback" ~ "nonadaptive_playback"
    )
  )

# Convert it to a factor 
summary_clean <- summary_clean %>%
  mutate(
    partner_type = factor(
      partner_type,
      levels = c(
        "no_partner",
        "adaptive_human",
        "adaptive_ai",
        "nonadaptive_playback"
      )
    )
  )

# Check 
table(summary_clean$partner_type)
```

```{r}
# 6. Converting phase to factor variable 
summary_clean <- summary_clean %>%
  mutate(
    phase = factor(
      phase,
      levels = c("approach", "homing_in"),
      labels = c("Approach", "Homing-in")
    )
  )

# Check
table(summary_clean$phase)
```

```{r}
# 7. Check contribution angles
table(summary_clean$contribution_angle)
```

```{r}
# 8. Making sure iteration is numeric for further analysis 
summary_clean <- summary_clean %>%
  mutate(
    iteration = as.numeric(iteration)
  )

# Check
glimpse(summary_clean)
```

```{r}
# 9. Add axis-control variable
frame_clean <- frame_clean %>%
  mutate(
    axis_control = case_when(
      
      # AI condition
      mode == "ai" & ai_axis == 1 ~ "AI_vertical",
      mode == "ai" & ai_axis == 0 ~ "AI_horizontal",
      
      # Playback condition
      mode == "playback" & playback_axis == "vertical" ~ "Playback_vertical",
      mode == "playback" & playback_axis == "horizontal" ~ "Playback_horizontal",
      
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# Convert to factor
frame_clean <- frame_clean %>%
  mutate(
    axis_control = factor(axis_control)
  )

# Check
table(frame_clean$axis_control, useNA = "ifany")
```

```{r}
# 10. Use logged dyad ID
summary_clean <- summary_clean %>%
  mutate(
    dyad_id = as.character(dyad_id),
    dyad_id = na_if(dyad_id, ""),
    dyad_id = factor(dyad_id)

# Check
table(summary_clean$dyad_id, useNA = "ifany")
```

```{r}
# 11. Create trial-level dataset
trial_data <- summary_clean %>%
  select(
    participant_id,
    dyad_id,
    mode,
    condition,
    partner_type,
    iteration,
    phase,
    target_angle,
    contribution_angle,
    reaction_time_s,
    distance_px,
    error_trial
  )

# Check
trial_data %>%
  count(condition, phase)

#This trial_data will be the main dataset for: RT analyses; DIST analyses; ANOVAs; t-tests; condition comparisons and learning analyses.
```

```{r}
# 12. Rename dependent variables for analysis
trial_data <- trial_data %>%
  rename(
    RT   = reaction_time_s,
    DIST = distance_px
  )

# Check
glimpse(trial_data)
```

```{r}
# 13. Remove error trials from RT/DIST analyses
analysis_data <- trial_data %>%
  filter(error_trial == FALSE)

# Check
table(analysis_data$error_trial)
```
Error-trial criteria: "Two types of behavior were classified as errors: If the cursor moved into the homing-in zone but then excited it again, and if the cursor moved outside of the screen borders." (Wahn at al., 2016)

```{r}
# 18. Calculate collective benefit (RT)

# Mean individual RT per participant
individual_RT <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(condition == "individual") %>%
  group_by(participant_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    individual_RT = mean(RT, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Mean cooperative RT per dyad
cooperative_RT <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(condition == "cooperative") %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    cooperative_RT = mean(RT, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Best individual within each dyad
#dyad mapping
participant_dyad_map <- tibble::tribble(
  ~participant_id, ~dyad_id,
   "666",         "666_����",
   "����",      "666_����",
   "august",      "august_jens",
   "jens",        "august_jens",
   "jakob",       "jakob_niels",
   "niels",       "jakob_niels",
   "odin",        "odin_line",
   "line",        "odin_line",
   "valeria",     "valeria_emil",
   "emil",        "valeria_emil",
   "lasse",       "mads_lasse",
   "mads",        "mads_lasse"
  
)

best_individual_RT <- individual_RT %>%
  left_join(participant_dyad_map, by = "participant_id") %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    best_individual_RT = min(individual_RT, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Calculate collective benefit
collective_benefit_RT <- cooperative_RT %>%
  left_join(
    best_individual_RT,
    by = c("dyad_id", "phase", "contribution_angle")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    collective_benefit = best_individual_RT / cooperative_RT
  )

# Check
glimpse(collective_benefit_RT)
```
```{r}
#Collective benefit DIST

individual_DIST <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(condition == "individual") %>%
  group_by(participant_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    individual_DIST = mean(DIST, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cooperative_DIST <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(condition == "cooperative") %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    cooperative_DIST = mean(DIST, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

#Best (lowest) individual DIST within each dyad
best_individual_DIST <- individual_DIST %>%
  left_join(participant_dyad_map, by = "participant_id") %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    best_individual_DIST = min(individual_DIST, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

#collective benefit (DIST)
collective_benefit_DIST <- cooperative_DIST %>%
  left_join(
    best_individual_DIST,
    by = c("dyad_id", "phase", "contribution_angle")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    collective_benefit = best_individual_DIST / cooperative_DIST
  )

#check
glimpse(collective_benefit_DIST)


```
Collective benefit interpretation: "Values above 1 indicate a collective benefit because dyad RT is lower than the faster member's RT. This measure was calculated separately for Approach and Homing-in phase - averaged across all contribution angles as well as separately for each of the three contribution angles (30%, 50%, 70%)"
- 0° and 90°: only one dyad member controls controls the cursor as only horizontal or vertical is required
- 45°: both members contributed equally - 50%
- 22.5° and 67.5°: one of the members contributed more than the other: 30% vs 70%

```{r}
# 19. Calculate skill ratio (RT)
skill_ratio_RT <- individual_RT %>%
  left_join(participant_dyad_map, by = "participant_id") %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    faster_partner = min(individual_RT, na.rm = TRUE),
    slower_partner = max(individual_RT, na.rm = TRUE),
    skill_ratio    = faster_partner / slower_partner,
    .groups = "drop"
  )
# Check
glimpse(skill_ratio_RT)
```

```{r}
#Skill ratio DIST
skill_ratio_DIST <- individual_DIST %>%
  left_join(participant_dyad_map, by = "participant_id") %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    faster_partner = min(individual_DIST, na.rm = TRUE),
    slower_partner = max(individual_DIST, na.rm = TRUE),
    skill_ratio    = faster_partner / slower_partner,
    .groups = "drop"
  )
# Check
glimpse(skill_ratio_DIST)
```
Skill ratio interpretation: A value of 1 indicates that both members perform equally well individually, whereas an increasingly lower ratio indicates a larger interindividual performance difference.

#INDIVIDUAL and COLLECTIVE analysis

```{r}
#correlating interindivual RT skill ratios with collective benefit for each of the contribution conditions, separately for Approach and Homing-in

#join the two into one data frame
corr_data <- collective_benefit_RT %>%
  left_join(skill_ratio_RT, by = c("dyad_id", "phase", "contribution_angle"))

#Pearson r between skill_ratio and collective benefit
correlation_results <- corr_data %>%
  group_by(phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(skill_ratio) & !is.na(collective_benefit)),
    r = cor(skill_ratio, collective_benefit, use = "complete.obs"),
    p_value = tryCatch(
      cor.test(skill_ratio, collective_benefit)$p.value,
      error = function(e) NA_real_
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sig = case_when(
      p_value < .001 ~ "***",
      p_value < .01  ~ "**",
      p_value < .05  ~ "*",
      p_value < .10  ~ "†",
      TRUE           ~ ""
    )
  )
print(correlation_results)

#plot
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(corr_data, aes(x = skill_ratio, y = collective_benefit)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.75, aes(colour = phase)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  facet_grid(phase ~ contribution_angle,
             labeller = labeller(
               contribution_angle = function(x) paste0(x, "°")
             )) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Approach" = "#4C9BE8", "Homing-in" = "#E8834C")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Skill ratio RT vs. collective benefit RT",
    subtitle = "Rows = phase  |  Columns = contribution angle",
    x        = "Skill ratio (best RT / worst RT)",
    y        = "Collective benefit (best individual RT / cooperative RT)",
    colour   = "Phase"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

```{r}
    ),

  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  facet_grid(phase ~ contribution_angle,
             labeller = labeller(
               contribution_angle = function(x) paste0(x, "°")
             )) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Approach" = "#4C9BE8", "Homing-in" = "#E8834C")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Skill ratio DIST vs. collective benefit DIST",
    subtitle = "Rows = phase  |  Columns = contribution angle",
    x        = "Skill ratio (best DIST / worst DIST)",
    y        = "Collective benefit (best individual DIST / cooperative DIST)",

  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```
Interpretation: Wahn et al. predicted that the collective benefit systematically increases with larger skill ratios, suggesting that dyad members who have increasingly similar individual performance levels benefit more from performing jointly - particularly when both members contribute equally to the joint performance. If however the better individual's dominance compensates for a larger interindividual difference (as in the 70% contribution condition (22.5° and 67.5°)), they predicted a reduced correlation relative to the other contribution conditions.
- With only 6 dyads, we have very low power per angle x phase cell, so we have to trat the correlations as descriptive/exploratory and flag that in the write-up (we could collapse across angles and just group by phase for more statistical power, but I don't think we should)

```{r}
#Checking for social facilitation
#Comparing RT in the individual and joint condition for the baseline angles 0° and 90°
#done separately for Approach and Homing-in

library(effectsize)

#filter to baseline angles
temp_sf <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(contribution_angle %in% c(0, 90),
         condition %in% c("individual", "cooperative")) %>%
  left_join(participant_dyad_map, by = "participant_id") %>%
  mutate(dyad_id = coalesce(dyad_id.x, dyad_id.y)) %>%
  select(-dyad_id.x, -dyad_id.y)

social_fac_data <- temp_sf %>%
  group_by(participant_id, dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle, condition) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_RT = mean(RT, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

#summary table
social_fac_summary <- social_fac_data %>%
  group_by(phase, contribution_angle, condition) %>%
  summarise(
    n     = n(),
    M_RT  = mean(mean_RT, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE_RT = sd(mean_RT, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
print(social_fac_summary)

#paired t-tests + Wilcoxon + Cohen's d per phase x angle

#individual: average both members per dyad
temp_ind <- social_fac_data %>%
  filter(condition == "individual") %>%
  left_join(participant_dyad_map, by = "participant_id") %>%
  mutate(dyad_id = coalesce(dyad_id.x, dyad_id.y)) %>%
  select(-dyad_id.x, -dyad_id.y)

individual_sf <- temp_ind %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(ind_RT = mean(mean_RT, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

#cooperative
cooperative_sf <- social_fac_data %>%
  filter(condition == "cooperative") %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(coop_RT = mean(mean_RT, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

#join and run both t-test and Wilcoxon with Cohen's d
sf_tests <- individual_sf %>%
  left_join(cooperative_sf, by = c("dyad_id", "phase", "contribution_angle")) %>%
  group_by(phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    n         = n(),
    M_ind     = mean(ind_RT,  na.rm = TRUE),
    M_coop    = mean(coop_RT, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_diff = mean(coop_RT - ind_RT, na.rm = TRUE),
    t_stat    = tryCatch(t.test(coop_RT, ind_RT, paired = TRUE)$statistic,  error = function(e) NA),
    t_p_value = tryCatch(t.test(coop_RT, ind_RT, paired = TRUE)$p.value,    error = function(e) NA),
    W_stat    = tryCatch(wilcox.test(coop_RT, ind_RT, paired = TRUE)$statistic, error = function(e) NA),
    W_p_value = tryCatch(wilcox.test(coop_RT, ind_RT, paired = TRUE)$p.value,   error = function(e) NA),
    cohens_d  = tryCatch(
      repeated_measures_d(coop_RT, ind_RT, method = "z")$d,
      error = function(e) NA
    ),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    t_sig = case_when(
      t_p_value < .001 ~ "***",
      t_p_value < .01  ~ "**",
      t_p_value < .05  ~ "*",
      t_p_value < .10  ~ "†",
      TRUE             ~ ""
    ),
    W_sig = case_when(
      W_p_value < .001 ~ "***",
      W_p_value < .01  ~ "**",
      W_p_value < .05  ~ "*",
      W_p_value < .10  ~ "†",
      TRUE             ~ ""
    )
  )
print(sf_tests)

#plot
temp_plot <- social_fac_data %>%
  left_join(participant_dyad_map, by = "participant_id") %>%
  mutate(dyad_id = coalesce(dyad_id.x, dyad_id.y)) %>%
  select(-dyad_id.x, -dyad_id.y)

temp_plot %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle, condition) %>%
  summarise(mean_RT = mean(mean_RT, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(contribution_angle = factor(paste0(contribution_angle, "°"),
                                     levels = c("0°", "90°"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = condition, y = mean_RT, colour = condition, group = dyad_id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.4, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "line",
               linewidth = 1.2, colour = "grey20") +
  stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "point",
               size = 4, shape = 18, colour = "grey20") +
  facet_grid(phase ~ contribution_angle) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("individual"  = "#4C9BE8",
                                 "cooperative" = "#E8834C")) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("individual"  = "Individual",
                               "cooperative" = "Cooperative")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Social facilitation check",
    subtitle = "Baseline angles only  |  Rows = phase  |  Columns = angle",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Mean RT (s)",
    colour   = "Condition"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```
Interpretation:

1. Approach phase: At 0°, there was no significant difference between individual and cooperative RT (W = 11, p = 1.000, d = 0.12). Similarly, at 90°, cooperative and individual RTs did not differ significantly (W = 9, p = .844, d = -0.19), with the small negative d indicating cooperative RT was marginally faster than individual.

2. Homing-in phase: At 0°, no significant difference was found between conditions (W = 13, p = .688, d = 0.05). At 90°, cooperative RT (M = 5.24 s) was notably slower than individual RT (M = 2.78 s), though this difference did not reach significance (W = 17, p = .219, d = 0.53), representing a medium effect size.

```{r}
#Checking for social facilitation
#Comparing DIST in the individual and joint condition for the baseline angles 0° and 90°
#done separately for Approach and Homing-in

library(effectsize)

#filter to baseline angles
temp_sf_dist <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(contribution_angle %in% c(0, 90),
         condition %in% c("individual", "cooperative")) %>%
  left_join(participant_dyad_map, by = "participant_id") %>%
  mutate(dyad_id = coalesce(dyad_id.x, dyad_id.y)) %>%
  select(-dyad_id.x, -dyad_id.y)

social_fac_data_dist <- temp_sf_dist %>%
  group_by(participant_id, dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle, condition) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_DIST = mean(DIST, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

#summary table
social_fac_summary_dist <- social_fac_data_dist %>%
  group_by(phase, contribution_angle, condition) %>%
  summarise(
    n       = n(),
    M_DIST  = mean(mean_DIST, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE_DIST = sd(mean_DIST, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
print(social_fac_summary_dist)

#paired t-tests + Wilcoxon + Cohen's d per phase x angle

#individual: average both members per dyad
temp_ind_dist <- social_fac_data_dist %>%
  filter(condition == "individual") %>%
  left_join(participant_dyad_map, by = "participant_id") %>%
  mutate(dyad_id = coalesce(dyad_id.x, dyad_id.y)) %>%
  select(-dyad_id.x, -dyad_id.y)

individual_sf_dist <- temp_ind_dist %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(ind_DIST = mean(mean_DIST, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

#cooperative
cooperative_sf_dist <- social_fac_data_dist %>%
  filter(condition == "cooperative") %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(coop_DIST = mean(mean_DIST, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

#join and run both t-test and Wilcoxon with Cohen's d
sf_tests_dist <- individual_sf_dist %>%
  left_join(cooperative_sf_dist, by = c("dyad_id", "phase", "contribution_angle")) %>%
  group_by(phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    n         = n(),
    M_ind     = mean(ind_DIST,  na.rm = TRUE),
    M_coop    = mean(coop_DIST, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_diff = mean(coop_DIST - ind_DIST, na.rm = TRUE),
    t_stat    = tryCatch(t.test(coop_DIST, ind_DIST, paired = TRUE)$statistic,      error = function(e) NA),
    t_p_value = tryCatch(t.test(coop_DIST, ind_DIST, paired = TRUE)$p.value,        error = function(e) NA),
    W_stat    = tryCatch(wilcox.test(coop_DIST, ind_DIST, paired = TRUE)$statistic, error = function(e) NA),
    W_p_value = tryCatch(wilcox.test(coop_DIST, ind_DIST, paired = TRUE)$p.value,   error = function(e) NA),
    cohens_d  = tryCatch(
      repeated_measures_d(coop_DIST, ind_DIST, method = "z")$d,
      error = function(e) NA
    ),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    t_sig = case_when(
      t_p_value < .001 ~ "***",
      t_p_value < .01  ~ "**",
      t_p_value < .05  ~ "*",
      t_p_value < .10  ~ "†",
      TRUE             ~ ""
    ),
    W_sig = case_when(
      W_p_value < .001 ~ "***",
      W_p_value < .01  ~ "**",
      W_p_value < .05  ~ "*",
      W_p_value < .10  ~ "†",
      TRUE             ~ ""
    )
  )
print(sf_tests_dist)

#plot
temp_plot_dist <- social_fac_data_dist %>%
  left_join(participant_dyad_map, by = "participant_id") %>%
  mutate(dyad_id = coalesce(dyad_id.x, dyad_id.y)) %>%
  select(-dyad_id.x, -dyad_id.y)

temp_plot_dist %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle, condition) %>%
  summarise(mean_DIST = mean(mean_DIST, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(contribution_angle = factor(paste0(contribution_angle, "°"),
                                     levels = c("0°", "90°"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = condition, y = mean_DIST, colour = condition, group = dyad_id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.4, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "line",
               linewidth = 1.2, colour = "grey20") +
  stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "point",
               size = 4, shape = 18, colour = "grey20") +
  facet_grid(phase ~ contribution_angle) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("individual"  = "#4C9BE8",
                                 "cooperative" = "#E8834C")) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("individual"  = "Individual",
                               "cooperative" = "Cooperative")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Social facilitation check (DIST)",
    subtitle = "Baseline angles only  |  Rows = phase  |  Columns = angle",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Mean DIST",
    colour   = "Condition"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```
Interpretation:

1. Approach: At 0°, dyads travelled slightly more distance cooperatively (M = 326) than individually (M = 305), a mean difference of 20.4 units, though this was non-significant (W = 11, p = .418, d = 0.42). At 90°, a similar pattern emerged — cooperative DIST (M = 330) exceeded individual DIST (M = 303) by 26.9 units, again non-significant (W = 9, p = .787, d = 0.30). Both effects are small-to-medium in size but in the direction of a coordination cost — dyads travel more than individuals.

2. Homing-in: At 0°, the pattern reverses: cooperative DIST (M = 300) was actually lower than individual DIST (M = 377), a mean difference of -76.6 units (W = 9, p = .844, d = -0.25). This hints at a slight collective benefit in path efficiency, though it is non-significant and small. At 90°, the largest effect emerges — cooperative DIST (M = 448) was 238 units greater than individual DIST (M = 209), a medium effect (d = 0.48) that nonetheless failed to reach significance (W = 18, p = .156), suggesting a meaningful coordination cost at maximal asymmetry during Homing-in.

```{r}
#2x3 Repeated measures ANOVA: phase x contribution angle

library(ez)

#RT

anova_data_RT <- collective_benefit_RT %>%
  filter(contribution_angle %in% c(22.5, 45, 67.5)) %>%

    phase               = factor(phase),
    contribution_angle  = factor(contribution_angle)

  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%

anova_RT <- ezANOVA(
  data       = anova_data_RT,
  dv         = collective_benefit,
  wid        = dyad_id,
  within     = .(phase, contribution_angle),
  type       = 3,
  detailed   = TRUE,

)
```

```{r}
#Steiger test for comparing correlations between angles both DIST and RT
library(cocor)

run_steiger <- function(corr_data, correlation_results, measure_label) {
  
  angles <- c(22.5, 45, 67.5)
  phases <- c("Approach", "Homing-in")
  
  # all pairs where 67.5° is compared to the other two
  comparisons <- list(
    c(67.5, 22.5),
    c(67.5, 45)
  )
  
  for (phase_label in phases) {
    
    d <- corr_data %>% filter(phase == phase_label)
    
    r_vals <- correlation_results %>%
      filter(phase == phase_label) %>%
      select(contribution_angle, r) %>%
      deframe()
    
    n <- d %>%
      filter(contribution_angle == angles[1]) %>%
      summarise(n = sum(!is.na(skill_ratio) & !is.na(collective_benefit))) %>%
      pull(n)
    
    get_r <- function(a1, a2) {
      x <- d %>% filter(contribution_angle == a1) %>% pull(collective_benefit)
      y <- d %>% filter(contribution_angle == a2) %>% pull(collective_benefit)
      cor(x, y, use = "complete.obs")
    }
    
    for (pair in comparisons) {
      a1 <- pair[1]; a2 <- pair[2]
      cat("\n======", measure_label, "|", phase_label, ":", a1, "° vs", a2, "° ======\n")
      print(cocor.dep.groups.overlap(
        r.jk = r_vals[as.character(a1)],
        r.jh = r_vals[as.character(a2)],
        r.kh = get_r(a1, a2),
        n    = n
      ))
    }
  }
}

#RT
run_steiger(corr_data, correlation_results, "RT")

#DIST
run_steiger(corr_data2, correlation_results2, "DIST")
```

```{r}
#Performance relative to individual baseline (RT and DIST)
ind_means_RT <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(condition == "individual") %>%
  group_by(participant_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(ind_RT = mean(RT, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ai_means_RT <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(condition == "ai") %>%
  group_by(participant_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(ai_RT = mean(RT, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

pb_means_RT <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(condition == "playback") %>%
  group_by(participant_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(pb_RT = mean(RT, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Ratio: individual / condition (>1 means condition is better) 
ratio_ai_RT <- ind_means_RT %>%
  inner_join(ai_means_RT, by = c("participant_id", "phase", "contribution_angle")) %>%
  mutate(ratio = ind_RT / ai_RT)

ratio_pb_RT <- ind_means_RT %>%
  inner_join(pb_means_RT, by = c("participant_id", "phase", "contribution_angle")) %>%
  mutate(ratio = ind_RT / pb_RT)

#one-sample t-test: is ratio different from 1?
run_ratio_tests <- function(df, ratio_col = "ratio", label) {
  df %>%
    group_by(phase, contribution_angle) %>%
    summarise(
      condition  = label,
      n          = sum(!is.na(.data[[ratio_col]])),
      M_ratio    = mean(.data[[ratio_col]], na.rm = TRUE),
      SE_ratio   = sd(.data[[ratio_col]], na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n),
      t_stat     = tryCatch(t.test(.data[[ratio_col]], mu = 1)$statistic, error = function(e) NA),
      p_value    = tryCatch(t.test(.data[[ratio_col]], mu = 1)$p.value,   error = function(e) NA),
      cohens_d   = tryCatch(
        (mean(.data[[ratio_col]], na.rm = TRUE) - 1) / sd(.data[[ratio_col]], na.rm = TRUE),
        error = function(e) NA
      ),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      sig = case_when(
        p_value < .001 ~ "***",
        p_value < .01  ~ "**",
        p_value < .05  ~ "*",
        p_value < .10  ~ "†",
        TRUE           ~ ""
      )
    )
}

ratio_tests_ai_RT <- run_ratio_tests(ratio_ai_RT, label = "AI")
```

```{r}
#Condition-contribution analysis (phase x contribution angle ANOVAs)
run_contribution_anova <- function(cond_label, dv_col, dv_name) {
  
  d <- analysis_data %>%
    filter(condition == cond_label,
           contribution_angle %in% c(0, 22.5, 45, 67.5, 90)) %>%
    group_by(participant_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
    summarise(dv = mean(.data[[dv_col]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(
      phase              = factor(phase),
      contribution_angle = factor(contribution_angle)
    )
  
  cat("\n══════", cond_label, "—", dv_name, "Phase × Contribution Angle ANOVA ══════\n")
  
  anova_out <- ezANOVA(
    data       = d,
    dv         = dv,
    wid        = participant_id,
    within     = .(phase, contribution_angle),
    type       = 3,
    detailed   = TRUE,
    return_aov = TRUE
  )
  print(anova_out)
  print(effectsize::eta_squared(anova_out$aov, partial = TRUE))
  
  #pairwise comparisons of contribution angle (collapsed over phase)
  cat("\n── Pairwise angle comparisons (Bonferroni) ──\n")
  pw_data <- d %>%
    group_by(participant_id, contribution_angle) %>%
    summarise(mean_dv = mean(dv, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  
  pw <- pairwise.t.test(
    x               = pw_data$mean_dv,
    g               = pw_data$contribution_angle,
    paired          = TRUE,
    p.adjust.method = "bonferroni"
  )
  print(pw)
  
  #plot
  p <- d %>%
    mutate(
      contribution_angle = factor(paste0(contribution_angle, "°"),
                                  levels = c("0°", "22.5°", "45°", "67.5°", "90°"))
    ) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = contribution_angle, y = dv, colour = phase, group = phase)) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.4, size = 2) +
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 4, shape = 18,
                 position = position_dodge(0.3)) +
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line", linewidth = 1,
                 position = position_dodge(0.3)) +
    stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.2,
                 position = position_dodge(0.3), linewidth = 0.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("Approach" = "#4C9BE8", "Homing-in" = "#E8834C")) +
    labs(
      title  = paste(cond_label, "–", dv_name, "by Phase × Contribution Angle"),
      x = "Contribution angle", y = dv_name, colour = "Phase"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
  
  print(p)
  invisible(list(anova = anova_out, pairwise = pw))
}

#RT
res_ai_RT  <- run_contribution_anova("ai",       "RT", "Mean RT (s)")
res_pb_RT  <- run_contribution_anova("playback", "RT", "Mean RT (s)")

#DIST
res_ai_DIST <- run_contribution_anova("ai",       "DIST", "Mean DIST (px)")
res_pb_DIST <- run_contribution_anova("playback", "DIST", "Mean DIST (px)")
```

```{r}
#Adaptiveness analysis - adaptive ai vs non-adaptive playback (for RT)

# AI vs Playback adaptiveness benefit: RT and DIST
ai_vs_pb <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(condition %in% c("ai", "playback")) %>%
  group_by(participant_id, condition, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_RT   = mean(RT,   na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_DIST = mean(DIST, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = condition,
    values_from = c(mean_RT, mean_DIST)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    adaptiveness_RT   = mean_RT_playback   / mean_RT_ai,    # >1 means AI faster
    adaptiveness_DIST = mean_DIST_playback / mean_DIST_ai   # >1 means AI shorter
  )

# One-sample t-tests vs 1 per phase × angle
adapt_tests <- ai_vs_pb %>%
  group_by(phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    n            = sum(!is.na(adaptiveness_RT)),
    M_RT         = mean(adaptiveness_RT,   na.rm = TRUE),
    SE_RT        = sd(adaptiveness_RT,     na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n),
    t_RT         = tryCatch(t.test(adaptiveness_RT,   mu = 1)$statistic, error = function(e) NA),
    p_RT         = tryCatch(t.test(adaptiveness_RT,   mu = 1)$p.value,   error = function(e) NA),
    d_RT         = (M_RT - 1) / sd(adaptiveness_RT, na.rm = TRUE),
    M_DIST       = mean(adaptiveness_DIST, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE_DIST      = sd(adaptiveness_DIST,   na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n),
    t_DIST       = tryCatch(t.test(adaptiveness_DIST, mu = 1)$statistic, error = function(e) NA),
    p_DIST       = tryCatch(t.test(adaptiveness_DIST, mu = 1)$p.value,   error = function(e) NA),
    d_DIST       = (M_DIST - 1) / sd(adaptiveness_DIST, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sig_RT   = case_when(p_RT   < .001 ~ "***", p_RT   < .01 ~ "**", p_RT   < .05 ~ "*", p_RT   < .10 ~ "†", TRUE ~ ""),
    sig_DIST = case_when(p_DIST < .001 ~ "***", p_DIST < .01 ~ "**", p_DIST < .05 ~ "*", p_DIST < .10 ~ "†", TRUE ~ "")
  )

print(adapt_tests)

# Plot 
adapt_long <- ai_vs_pb %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(adaptiveness_RT, adaptiveness_DIST),
    names_to  = "dv",
    values_to = "benefit"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    dv = factor(dv,
                levels = c("adaptiveness_RT", "adaptiveness_DIST"),
                labels = c("RT ratio", "DIST ratio")),
    contribution_angle = factor(paste0(contribution_angle, "°"),
                                levels = c("0°", "22.5°", "45°", "67.5°", "90°"))
  )

adapt_tests_long <- adapt_tests %>%
  mutate(contribution_angle = factor(paste0(contribution_angle, "°"),
                                     levels = c("0°", "22.5°", "45°", "67.5°", "90°"))) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(sig_RT, sig_DIST),
    names_to  = "dv",
    values_to = "sig"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    dv      = factor(dv,
                     levels = c("sig_RT", "sig_DIST"),
                     labels = c("RT ratio", "DIST ratio")),
    y_pos   = ifelse(dv == "RT ratio",
                     max(ai_vs_pb$adaptiveness_RT,   na.rm = TRUE) + 0.1,
                     max(ai_vs_pb$adaptiveness_DIST, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.1)
  )

ggplot(adapt_long, aes(x = contribution_angle, y = benefit, colour = phase)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.5, size = 2,
              position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.1, dodge.width = 0.4)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 4, shape = 18,
               position = position_dodge(0.4)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line", aes(group = phase),
               position = position_dodge(0.4), linewidth = 0.8) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.2,
               position = position_dodge(0.4), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_text(data = adapt_tests_long,
            aes(x = contribution_angle, y = y_pos, label = sig, colour = phase),
            position = position_dodge(0.4), size = 5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(dv ~ phase, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Approach" = "#4C9BE8", "Homing-in" = "#E8834C")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Adaptiveness benefit: Playback / AI",
    subtitle = "Dashed line = no benefit  |  >1 = AI outperforms playback",
    x = "Contribution angle", y = "Ratio", colour = "Phase"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```
Interpretation:
The results of the condition-contribution analysis and the adaptiveness analysis look very similar but there are key differences:

 - Condition-contribution analysis: For each condition (AI, playback) separately, it just takes the raw mean RT/DIST at each contribution angle and phase, runs an ANOVA to see if angle and phase affect performance, and plots those means. It describes the shape of performance across angles within each condition.
 
 - Adaptiveness benefit: Takes the ratio of playback/AI at each matched angle and phase within the same participant, so it's a direct within-person measure of what the AI's adaptiveness buys you over a non-adaptive partner doing the exact same movements. Values above 1 mean the AI condition was faster/shorter than playback.
 
- Human cooperative mode had to be taken out here because their data is grouped (it belongs to 2 people instead of just one) and therefore cannot be added to the analysis here
 
```{r}
#for AI and playback: average the two dyad members per dyad as baseline
#for cooperative: best dyad member is used as baseline
cb_ai_dyad_RT <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(condition == "ai") %>%
  left_join(participant_dyad_map, by = "participant_id") %>%
  rename(dyad_id = dyad_id.y) %>%
  filter(!is.na(dyad_id)) %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(part_RT = mean(RT, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(best_individual_RT, by = c("dyad_id", "phase", "contribution_angle")) %>%
  mutate(collective_benefit = best_individual_RT / part_RT,
         partner_type = "adaptive_ai")

cb_pb_dyad_RT <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(condition == "playback") %>%
  left_join(participant_dyad_map, by = "participant_id") %>%
  rename(dyad_id = dyad_id.y) %>%
  filter(!is.na(dyad_id)) %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(part_RT = mean(RT, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(best_individual_RT, by = c("dyad_id", "phase", "contribution_angle")) %>%
  mutate(collective_benefit = best_individual_RT / part_RT,
         partner_type = "nonadaptive_playback")

cb_coop_dyad_RT <- collective_benefit_RT %>%
  mutate(partner_type = "adaptive_human")

#bind all three — now all at dyad level, n = 6 each
cb_all_dyad_RT <- bind_rows(
  cb_coop_dyad_RT %>% select(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle, collective_benefit, partner_type),
  cb_ai_dyad_RT,
  cb_pb_dyad_RT
) %>%
  mutate(
    partner_type = factor(partner_type,
                          levels = c("adaptive_human", "adaptive_ai", "nonadaptive_playback")),
    contribution_angle = factor(paste0(contribution_angle, "°"),
                                levels = c("0°", "22.5°", "45°", "67.5°", "90°"))
  )

#pairwise comparisons per phase (paired by dyad)
for (ph in levels(cb_all_dyad_RT$phase)) {
  cat("\n── Phase:", ph, "──\n")
  d <- cb_all_dyad_RT %>% filter(phase == ph) %>%
    group_by(dyad_id, partner_type) %>%
    summarise(mean_cb = mean(collective_benefit, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  print(pairwise.t.test(
    x               = d$mean_cb,
    g               = d$partner_type,
    paired          = TRUE,
    p.adjust.method = "bonferroni"
  ))
}

#plot
ggplot(cb_all_dyad_RT,
       aes(x = contribution_angle, y = collective_benefit, colour = partner_type)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.5, size = 2,
              position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.1, dodge.width = 0.5)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 4, shape = 18,
               position = position_dodge(0.5)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line", aes(group = partner_type),
               position = position_dodge(0.5), linewidth = 0.8) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.2,
               position = position_dodge(0.5), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(~ phase) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("adaptive_human"       = "#E8834C",
               "adaptive_ai"          = "#9B59B6",
               "nonadaptive_playback" = "#27AE60"),
    labels = c("Adaptive Human", "Adaptive AI", "Non-adaptive Playback")
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Collective benefit (RT) by partner type",
    subtitle = "Dyad-level comparison, n = 6  |  Dashed line = no benefit over individual",
    x = "Contribution angle", y = "Collective benefit (individual / condition RT)",
    colour = "Partner type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```
Now all three conditions are at dyad level with the same n = 6, so the paired t-tests are valid — each dyad contributes one observation per condition. Flag in the write-up that the cooperative collective benefit uses the better of the two members as the individual baseline, while AI and playback average across both members, which is a slight asymmetry.

We use the best individual performance of the two dyad members as the baseline for all three conditions, we accept the small asymmetry in the write-up, and note that a human-contribution-only reconstruction would require frame-level simulation beyond the scope of the current analysis.

```{r}
       aes(x = contribution_angle, y = collective_benefit, colour = partner_type)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.5, size = 2,
              position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.1, dodge.width = 0.5)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 4, shape = 18,
               position = position_dodge(0.5)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line", aes(group = partner_type),
               position = position_dodge(0.5), linewidth = 0.8) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.2,
               position = position_dodge(0.5), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(~ phase) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("adaptive_human"       = "#E8834C",
               "adaptive_ai"          = "#9B59B6",
               "nonadaptive_playback" = "#27AE60"),
    labels = c("Adaptive Human", "Adaptive AI", "Non-adaptive Playback")
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Collective benefit (DIST) by partner type",
    subtitle = "Dyad-level comparison, n = 6  |  Dashed line = no benefit over individual",
    x = "Contribution angle", y = "Collective benefit (individual / condition DIST)",
    colour = "Partner type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

Within the AI and playback conditions separately, and within each phase, does a participant's average reaction time depend on whether their (artificial) partner was assigned the horizontal or the vertical axis?

```{r}
#Axis-control analysis RT
#join frame_clean axis_control variable to summary trial data

axis_trial <- frame_clean %>%
  mutate(mode = tolower(mode)) %>%
  filter(mode %in% c("ai", "playback")) %>%
  group_by(participant_id, mode, iteration, phase) %>%
  summarise(axis_control = first(na.omit(axis_control)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(phase = str_replace_all(tolower(phase), "[^a-z0-9]+", "_"))   

# analysis_data side: identical normalization before the join
analysis_axis <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(condition %in% c("ai", "playback")) %>%
  mutate(
    condition = as.character(condition),
    phase     = str_replace_all(tolower(as.character(phase)), "[^a-z0-9]+", "_")  
  ) %>%
  left_join(axis_trial %>% rename(condition = mode),
            by = c("participant_id", "condition", "iteration", "phase")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(axis_control)) %>%
  mutate(
    partner_axis = case_when(
      str_detect(axis_control, regex("horiz", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "horizontal",
      str_detect(axis_control, regex("vert",  ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "vertical",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    partner_axis = factor(partner_axis, levels = c("horizontal", "vertical"))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(partner_axis))

#participant-level means by condition × phase × axis
axis_means_RT <- analysis_axis %>%
  group_by(participant_id, condition, phase, partner_axis) %>%
  summarise(mean_RT = mean(RT, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

#paired t-test + Cohen's d: horizontal vs vertical within each condition × phase
axis_tests_RT <- axis_means_RT %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = partner_axis, values_from = mean_RT) %>%
  group_by(condition, phase) %>%
  summarise(
    n         = sum(!is.na(horizontal) & !is.na(vertical)),
    M_horiz   = mean(horizontal, na.rm = TRUE),
    M_vert    = mean(vertical,   na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_diff = mean(vertical - horizontal, na.rm = TRUE),
    t_stat    = tryCatch(t.test(vertical[!is.na(vertical) & !is.na(horizontal)],
                                horizontal[!is.na(vertical) & !is.na(horizontal)],
                                paired = TRUE)$statistic, error = function(e) NA),
    p_value   = tryCatch(t.test(vertical[!is.na(vertical) & !is.na(horizontal)],
                                horizontal[!is.na(vertical) & !is.na(horizontal)],
                                paired = TRUE)$p.value, error = function(e) NA),
    cohens_d  = tryCatch(
      mean(vertical - horizontal, na.rm = TRUE) /
        sd(vertical - horizontal,  na.rm = TRUE),
      error = function(e) NA
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sig = case_when(
      p_value < .001 ~ "***",
      p_value < .01  ~ "**",
      p_value < .05  ~ "*",
      p_value < .10  ~ "†",
      TRUE           ~ ""
    )
  )

cat("── Axis-control tests (RT) ──\n")
print(axis_tests_RT)

#plot
axis_means_RT %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = partner_axis, y = mean_RT, colour = partner_axis)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.5, size = 2) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 4, shape = 18) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_grid(phase ~ condition) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("horizontal" = "#3498DB", "vertical" = "#E74C3C")) +
  labs(
    title  = "RT by Axis Control (Horizontal vs Vertical)",
    x = "Partner axis", y = "Mean RT (s)", colour = "Axis"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

#Run learning analysis

The approach: for each cooperative trial, collective benefit is computed as the dyad's reaction time on that trial relative to the fixed best-individual baseline for the relevant contribution angle. Trial order within each dyad and phase is then entered as a continuous predictor in a linear mixed model with a random intercept and slope per dyad, so a positive trial slope indicates that collective benefit grows with practice (i.e. learning). Because there are only a handful of cooperative trials per contribution angle, trials are pooled across angle (the angle-specific baseline keeps the measure comparable) and binned only for the plot.inear mixed model with block as the learning predictor and a random effect per dyad.

The question behind it: do dyads get better at working together the more they practise? --> "better together" here menas that their joint performance beats what the stronger of the two could do alone (the collective benefit). 

Interpretation for the plots: we divide the cooperative RT/DIST by the better member's RT/DIST --> above 1: the pair did better than the better individual, below 1: the pair did worse than the better individual. Plots: dashed line at 1 means no benefit, it chops the trials into 4 chunks from early to late trials.

```{r}
#Run learning analysis
#does collective benefit (RT) grow over cooperative trials?

library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)   

#Per-trial collective benefit for the cooperative condition 
#numerator   = fixed best-individual baseline
#denominator = the dyad's RT on that single cooperative trial
coop_trials_RT <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(condition == "cooperative") %>%
  left_join(best_individual_RT, by = c("dyad_id", "phase", "contribution_angle")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(best_individual_RT), !is.na(RT), RT > 0) %>%
  mutate(cb_trial = best_individual_RT / RT)

#re-index trials chronologically within each dyad x phase, then center & scale
coop_trials_RT <- coop_trials_RT %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase) %>%
  arrange(iteration, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(trial_order = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    trial_z = as.numeric(scale(trial_order)),   # stabilises the random slope
    phase   = factor(phase)
  )

#Learning model: trial order predicting collective benefit ------------------
#continuous trial predictor, random intercept + slope per dyad
m_learn <- lmer(cb_trial ~ trial_z * phase + (trial_z | dyad_id), data = coop_trials_RT)
summary(m_learn)


#plot: block means across the experiment, per phase
n_blocks <- 4   # blocks are for the PLOT only; the model above uses raw trial order

cb_blocks_RT <- coop_trials_RT %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase) %>%
  mutate(block = ntile(trial_order, n_blocks)) %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, block) %>%
  summarise(collective_benefit = mean(cb_trial, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(cb_blocks_RT, aes(block, collective_benefit, colour = phase, fill = phase)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line", linewidth = 1) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 2.5) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, geom = "ribbon", alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Approach" = "#4C9BE8", "Homing-in" = "#E8834C")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values   = c("Approach" = "#4C9BE8", "Homing-in" = "#E8834C")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:n_blocks) +
  labs(
    title  = "Learning: collective benefit (RT) across cooperative trials",
    x      = paste0("Trial block (1\u2013", n_blocks, ")"),
    y      = "Collective benefit (RT min / RT dyad)",
    colour = "Phase", fill = "Phase"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
```{r}
# Run learning analysis: does collective benefit (DIST) grow over cooperative trials?

library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)   

#per-trial collective benefit (DIST) for the cooperative condition 
#numerator   = fixed best-individual DIST baseline (angle-specific)
#denominator = the dyad's DIST on that single cooperative trial
coop_trials_DIST <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(condition == "cooperative") %>%
  left_join(best_individual_DIST, by = c("dyad_id", "phase", "contribution_angle")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(best_individual_DIST), !is.na(DIST), DIST > 0) %>%
  mutate(cb_trial = best_individual_DIST / DIST)

#re-index trials chronologically within each dyad x phase, then center & scale
coop_trials_DIST <- coop_trials_DIST %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase) %>%
  arrange(iteration, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(trial_order = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    trial_z = as.numeric(scale(trial_order)),   # stabilises the random slope
    phase   = factor(phase)
  )

#Learning model: trial order predicting collective benefit (DIST)
m_learn_DIST <- lmer(cb_trial ~ trial_z * phase + (trial_z | dyad_id), data = coop_trials_DIST)
summary(m_learn_DIST)

#Plot: block means across the experiment, per phase

n_blocks <- 4   # blocks are for the PLOT only; the model above uses raw trial order

cb_blocks_DIST <- coop_trials_DIST %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase) %>%
  mutate(block = ntile(trial_order, n_blocks)) %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, block) %>%
  summarise(collective_benefit = mean(cb_trial, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(cb_blocks_DIST, aes(block, collective_benefit, colour = phase, fill = phase)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line", linewidth = 1) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 2.5) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, geom = "ribbon", alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Approach" = "#4C9BE8", "Homing-in" = "#E8834C")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values   = c("Approach" = "#4C9BE8", "Homing-in" = "#E8834C")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:n_blocks) +
  labs(
    title  = "Learning: collective benefit (DIST) across cooperative trials",
    x      = paste0("Trial block (1\u2013", n_blocks, ")"),
    y      = "Collective benefit (DIST min / DIST dyad)",
    colour = "Phase", fill = "Phase"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
